As we wrap up our journey down the River of Doubt, let’s take a moment to soak in what this story really means for us. This isn’t just an adventure story about Theodore Roosevelt, Kermit, Rondon, and their companions. It’s a powerful reminder of what it looks like to face the unknown, to hang on through hardship, and to come out the other side changed for the better. Think about it—how often do you feel lost or overwhelmed, not sure where the next step will lead? Their journey is a mirror for any of us who’ve ever been there. Here’s what I hope you’ll carry with you:
True leadership isn’t about going it alone. It’s about sharing the load and listening to people who see things differently. Humility isn’t a sign of weakness—it’s actually the root of real courage and growth. And endurance? It isn’t built in the big, heroic moments, but in those small, relentless steps you take every single day. The connections we make when times get tough—they’re strong enough to last through just about anything. And let’s not forget, nature’s sheer power reminds us there are forces bigger than ourselves—things we can’t always control or fully understand. If you ever find yourself up against your own “river of doubt”—maybe it’s a challenge that feels impossible, or a time when you’re not sure you can keep going—remember, you’re not alone. The road ahead might look uncertain. It might even ask more of you than you think you have to give. But just like Roosevelt and his team discovered, strength shows up in places you don’t expect—in the encouragement of others, in your ability to adapt, and in the quiet determination to keep moving, step by step. So, whenever you face hardship, try to see it not as an ending, but as the start of something deeper—a chance for growth, for connection, and for new wisdom. Trust in yourself. Lean into the support around you. And know that, even when things seem darkest, hope still flows—steady and quiet—like a river winding through the unknown. Whatever your next challenge is, you’ve got what it takes to meet it. Keep moving forward.
